items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So the band was very well integrated, a tremendous bunch of fellows: Zoot Sims, Jimmy Maxwell, Johnny Frosk.

ctx.x: How did you get to be a part of it?

Benny was putting together an orchestra. They wanted the orchestra integrated. He had called Joe Newman and me, and Teddy Wilson. Joya Sherrill was the vocalist with us. So the band was very well integrated, a tremendous bunch of fellows: Zoot Sims, Jimmy Maxwell, Johnny Frosk. We had a great bunch of guys. That was an interesting trip. It was very fascinating for most of us, because we didn’t know what to expect. We had been told – coached by the State Department. Don’t take any pictures from bridges. Don’t take…

course wanting to take pictures of everything I’d see. It got to the point where you just had to be very careful. And yet, the Russians themselves were not as – they weren’t as mean about it as we had been led to believe. Because I was going across the Volga River, by the Kremlin. I was in a taxi cab. I said, “Can I take a picture from there?” – the gestures I made. He said, “I don’t know.” He pulled over the cab. There was a policeman on the bridge. He asked him, and the cop said go ahead. I took some pictures.…

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: We were doing “Juke Box Saturday Night.” ... Johnny Frosk stood up and played “In the Mood” or something.

ctx.x: happened. This came out of one of those anecdote books. Are you familiar with a fellow named John Frosk?
And there was some incident — Glenn Osser was conducting something for Cyd Charisse or something, and apparently he called “In the Mood.”
